feed.title: Wits AHEAD · Daily briefing
feed.subtitle: News, research, video and things to read on AI, data and human capability for higher education.
feed.rights: Wits AHEAD Research Group, Wits School of Education, University of the Witwatersrand

entry.title: Joining up AI across recruitment, retention and alumni relations can close graduation gaps, if it is governed well
entry.summary:
Writing for University World News, IREX project director Cameron Mirza argue say universities suppose treat recruitment, retention and alumni relations as one connected, AI supported lifecycle instead of separate systems wey get separate data. E cite Georgia State University chatbot and predictive analytics programme, wey dem credit say e don cut "summer melt" by about 21 percent and don help Black, Hispanic, first generation and low income students graduate for rates wey match or pass di wider student body, but e warn say models wey dem train with historical data fit still entrench di inequities wey dem suppose fix.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and predictive analytics for student success, dis piece na good reminder say early-warning and retention tools go only close equity gap if dem pair am with human oversight and bias testing, na di same governance question Wits AHEAD dey ask for any analytics tool wey e recommend.

University World News · Established higher education press (commentary by a sector practitioner)

entry.title: Wits researchers argue Africa must set its own AI research agenda, not just apply others' tools
entry.summary:
Two computer scientists for University of di Witwatersrand, Benjamin Rosman and Steve James, wey dey co-direct di Robotics, Autonomous Intelligence and Learning (RAIL) Lab, dey argue say Africa suppose drive artificial intelligence research instead of just dey use tools wey dem build for oda places. Dem point to Deep Learning Indaba, wey don become di world biggest AI summer school, wey bring 1,300 participants go last year gathering for Kigali, and wey dey run im IndabaX programme for 48 out of Africa 54 kontris dis year, plus Wits new Machine Intelligence and Neural Discovery (MIND) Institute, wey bring togeda around 65 academics across computer science, neuroscience, psychology and policy.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, di warning against Africa becoming just "a place where oda people dey do science" dey speak straight to Wits AHEAD own mission to build African led capability to set AI research questions, no be just to use AI tools wey dem design for oda places.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: Study of students in China, Japan and Mongolia finds access to generative AI does not guarantee it is useful for learning
entry.summary:
One working paper wey study 42 undergraduates for one university each for China, Japan and Mongolia find out say how students dey reach generative AI, directly, through global platforms, or by switching language, dey shape whether e dey really useful for dem, no be just weda dem fit access am. Mongolian students, for example, often switch to English when Mongolian language outputs no reach standard, while all three groups weigh accuracy, privacy, dependence and how di tool dey affect dia own critical thinking. Di authors, Ming Li, Qin Xie, Ariunaa Enkhtur, Lilan Chen and Fei Cheng, conclude say technological access alone no guarantee equal educational use across different language and technology settings.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on generative AI for higher education, di finding say language and local technology conditions, no be connectivity alone, dey decide whether generative AI truly dey help students learn na warning Wits AHEAD dey apply di same way to English-dominant AI tools wey dem dey use across multilingual Southern African campuses.

arXiv (working paper) · Working paper (preprint, not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: South African minister tells universities to move from AI debate to decisions on teaching and research
entry.summary:
For di 4th Universities South Africa Higher Education Conference wey hold on 7 October 2026, South Africa Minister of Higher Education and Training, Buti Manamela, tell universities say artificial intelligence dey make dia main work, wey be to teach critical thinking and make people take responsibility for knowledge, important well well, no be less important, bikos AI systems fit produce confident content without check if e dey true. E add say di real question no be only wetin students dey use AI do for assignment, na who build di technology, whose language and experience e dey show, who dey control di infrastructure and who dey benefit, and e call for humanities and social sciences to work togeda wit engineering and natural sciences on di bias, power and labour wahala wey AI fit bring.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on generative AI for higher education, as one cabinet minister come dey lay out clear agenda for teaching, assessment and research capacity instead of just general argument, e dey give South African universities clear mandate to act on.

South African Government News Agency (SAnews) · National government news agency

entry.title: UNESCO study finds 87% of Latin American and Caribbean universities already use AI, but only 26% have a formal strategy
entry.summary:
One UNESCO IESALC working paper wit UNU-IAS, wey survey 200 higher education institutions across 19 Latin American and Caribbean kontris between August and October 2025, find out say 87 percent don already dey use AI for at least one area, lead by teaching and learning (74 percent) and research (57 percent), but only 26 percent get formal AI strategy and 55 percent no get dedicated AI budget at all. Adoption and governance dey follow institutional type well well: 84 percent of private non-profit universities dey use AI against 68 percent of public universities, and 17 percent of public universities report say dem no get staff training at all, against 3 percent of private non-profit ones.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, di finding say AI use don already spread wide while formal governance dey lag far behind, and e no balance across public and private institutions, dey mirror di governance gap Wits AHEAD dey see across di wider Global South.

UNESCO IESALC and UNU-IAS, reported by Times Higher Education · Established higher education press, reporting a UNESCO/UNU-IAS working paper

entry.title: UTeach survey finds STEM teacher-training staff cautiously optimistic about AI but wary of integrity and bias risks
entry.summary:
One survey of 57 faculty, administrators and staff from 31 university-based secondary STEM teacher-training programmes across 54 colleges and universities for United States find out say 77 percent agree say AI fit affect dia work well well, and 61 percent call demsef proactive adopters. 63 percent still worry about challenges, mostly academic integrity (42 percent) and ethical bias (21 percent), and 70 percent talk say dem need more training; 79 percent of instructors already dey use AI for dia courses, mostly for lesson planning and assessment design instead of data-heavy STEM inquiry.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, di gap between faculty wey don already dey try AI and di shared, research-based framework wey dem talk say dem no get, na exactly di kain structured guidance teacher-training programmes across Global South go also need.

The UTeach Institute, The University of Texas at Austin · University research institute report

entry.title: Systematic review finds no existing framework yet addresses the ethical and instructional challenges of AI in STEM teaching
entry.summary:
One systematic review by researchers for Wentworth Institute of Technology and di University of New Haven check established frameworks like TPACK, SAMR, ADDIE and Universal Design for Learning against AI literacy models and principles of responsible AI, to see how well dem fit support STEM instructors teaching practice. Dem find out say none of dis frameworks don address di professional, ethical and instructional challenges of using AI for STEM education, and say adoption of AI tools dey outpace systematic pedagogical guidance, wey make am tool-driven instead of framework-driven practice.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, di finding say no current instructional framework cover AI ethical and pedagogical wahala dey strengthen di case for di group own work on responsible, STEM-specific AI integration.

American Society for Engineering Education (ASEE), North East Section Conference · Peer-reviewed conference paper

entry.title: More universities end Turnitin contracts as concerns mount
entry.summary:
Times Higher Education report say Newcastle University and University of Westminster don join University of Southampton to end dia contract wit Turnitin, di plagiarism-detection company, afta Turnitin propose licence changes wey fit make dem use student coursework to train AI tools. Newcastle mention dat data clause direct; Westminster talk say Turnitin plagiarism checker 'largely ineffective' against AI-written text, and dia AI detector get 'a recognised risk of false positives'. Southampton alone pay Turnitin £87,621 for one year, out of student population wey pass 17,000 undergraduates and 8,000 postgraduates.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, dis matter show say universities dey start to weigh data governance and how reliable AI-detection tools really be against cost, instead of treating plagiarism-checking contract as something wey must dey fixed forever.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: Prepare students for post-graduation AI judgement challenges
entry.summary:
University World News talk say di way higher education dey respond to generative AI dey stop too early, for graduation time, wen di real test of professional judgement go come afta. Dem cite one 2026 field experiment wey dem register beforehand, inside di journal Organization Science, wia 758 Boston Consulting Group consultants do real-life work wit or witout generative AI assistant: for most of di tasks, di ones wey use AI work faster and better, but for one task wey pass wetin di tool fit do, na only 70.6% of di AI-assisted consultants get di correct answer, against 84.5% for dose wey work witout AI, and di graders wey no know di answer rate di wrong AI-assisted recommendations as convincing as di correct ones.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, dis finding wey show say confident but wrong AI-assisted work fit read as convincing as correct work dey point to professional judgement, no be AI literacy alone, as di capability wey graduates need well-well before dem enter di job market.

University World News · Established higher education press, commentary citing a peer-reviewed field experiment

entry.title: UNESCO and Codemao's AI coding drive reaches more African classrooms
entry.summary:
UNESCO and Chinese coding platform Codemao talk say di joint youth coding initiative dey continue to grow for Africa. Di second phase, wey go run reach 2030, don already train 200 teachers for Republic of Congo, Kenya, Namibia and Thailand, 45% of dem na women, and Kenya don get 200 tablets for 20 junior secondary schools.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, dis initiative show one way wey dem fit build AI and coding skill among teachers for Global South, wit special focus on women.

Xinhua (New China TV) · Major international news agency, video report

entry.title: PISA 2025 finds AI chatbot use split with student learning outcomes
entry.summary:
Di first PISA 2025 test from OECD wey check how students dey use AI, ask over 760,000 students wey dey 15 years old for 91 countries. Dem find out say students wey dey depend too much on AI chatbot to write dia assignment get lower science score, while students wey dey use AI small-small wit guidance show different and better pattern; reading and maths score sef don drop well-well for OECD countries for di past ten years.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI wey dey generate content for higher education, teaching, assessment and integrity, dis one na early sign of di habit wey students go carry come university, and wetin university go need teach and assess.

OECD (via Newsweek) · Intergovernmental body's flagship international assessment, reported by established press

entry.title: Understanding ethical dimensions of AI in higher education: insights from faculty members and students
entry.summary:
One study wey mix different research methods ask 971 students and 135 lecturers, den interview 23 students and 14 lecturers, about AI ethics for higher education. Both groups agree generally say dem must use AI well-well, but dia views differ: lecturers talk say ethics matter well but dia schools no get clear guidelines, while students see AI as something wey dey help dem learn but dem no sure where dia own responsibility stop.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI wey get responsibility, ethics, equity and policy, di study recommendations, lecturer training, special ethics courses and clear university guidelines, give practical checklist for institutions wey never get formal AI ethics policy.

International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: From AI literacy to action: South Africa charts a path forward for teacher education
entry.summary:
South Africa Department of Higher Education and Training and Commonwealth of Learning hold one national workshop wey last two days on AI for teacher education, for University of Pretoria Future Africa campus. Teachers, policy people and system leaders agree on one flexible national policy wey dey based on principles, dem form one national task team, make di result feed into di ongoing review of di Minimum Requirements for Teacher Education Qualifications, wey di people wey dey attend talk say no dey mention AI at all now.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, dis one show clear process, wey government dey lead, wey turn AI literacy to national qualification policy for South Africa teacher education system.

Commonwealth of Learning · Intergovernmental organisation report on a national government workshop

entry.title: Supporting cost-effective AI adoption in education
entry.summary:
World Bank don publish one working paper, Costing AI Use in Education in Low- and Middle-Income Countries, wit one blog post wey explain how ministries of education suppose budget for AI. E recommend say make dem start wit tools wey go help teachers, like lesson planning and feedback, instead of to roll am out to all students one time, make dem compare AI cost wit di cost wey dem dey spend now to expand normal teaching, and make dem use devices and mobile networks wey already dey schools. World Bank estimate say to reach di sustainable development goal for education for Sub-Saharan Africa go need extra six point four billion US dollars every year for primary school teachers and thirty-eight point seven billion dollars every year for secondary school teachers by 2030.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on analytics and data wey dey help education systems and decision-making, dis report give ministries and institutions for Global South one clear framework wey show di cost, to help dem decide where AI spending for education go do di most good.

World Bank · Intergovernmental body blog, summarising a World Bank working paper

entry.title: Grappling with "homework scams", US universities shun AI detectors
entry.summary:
One AFP report wey eNCA carry explain how Yale, Cornell and University of Wisconsin-Madison dey discourage or ban dia staff from use AI detection software as evidence of cheating, after studies find out say di tools no dey reliable and dem dey often flag innocent pipo wrongly, including pipo wey no be native English speaker. One biology lecturer for Wisconsin-Madison, wey hide one instruction inside assignment, catch 60 out of 350 students wey dey use AI without normal check dey see dem, and e dey move go oral exam and video debate instead of essay; one survey from American Association of Colleges and Universities and Elon University find out say 95% of lecturers dey fear say students dey depend too much on AI.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Generative AI for higher education, especially assessment and academic integrity, na di first pillar of Wits AHEAD, and dis one wey big universities dey waka commot from AI detection software na direct, practical sign for how di group suppose advise on assessment redesign instead of detection as answer to AI misuse.

AFP (via eNCA) · Established press (wire service report)

entry.title: Global Employment Trends for Youth 2026: Back to the Future
entry.summary:
Di International Labour Organization report, Global Employment Trends for Youth 2026, find out say world youth unemployment rate rise reach 12.4% for 2025, dis one leave around 67 million young pipo wey dia age dey between 15 to 24 without work, while around one out of five young pipo, around 257 million, no dey work, no dey school, and no dey train. Di report estimate say 6.1% of work wey young pipo wey dia age dey between 15 to 29 dey do fit face big risk from AI dey take over dia task, mostly office and clerical work wey don already dey shrink for young workers, and e dey call for human centred way to govern AI and technology, alongside more support to decent work.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Graduate employability and just transitions, including how AI dey change entry level work, na di fourth pillar of Wits AHEAD, and dis one wey dis intergovernmental report find out, say office work, wey often be first step for graduate, dey face di most risk from AI, give di group one concrete, global benchmark for dia work on AI and graduate employability for Global South.

International Labour Organization · Intergovernmental body report

entry.title: Generative AI use and misuse call for assessment reform in higher education
entry.summary:
One peer-reviewed study for di journal Science survey over 95,000 students for 20 big public research university for United States, for di 2023-24 school year. Dem find out say 37% of students dey use generative AI at least once every month for assignment, and di authors estimate say around 9% use am to cheat, dis one dey rise reach 26% among pipo wey dey use am every day; how pipo dey use am and dey cheat dey different well well according to course of study. Di authors talk say make dem change how dem dey assess student according to each course, instead of blanket ban or detection system for di whole university.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Generative AI for higher education, especially assessment and academic integrity, na di first pillar of Wits AHEAD, and dis big study wey show say misuse dey different according to course, no be di same everywhere, give di group real evidence to design assessment change wey dey fit each course, instead of one blanket change.

Science · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: UCT summit puts AI, inequality and future of universities in spotlight
entry.summary:
Di Times Higher Education World Academic Summit open for University of Cape Town on 30 September 2026, na di first time dis summit dey happen for Africa. Around 600 higher education leaders, academics and policy makers from more than 60 kontris come join; di Vice-Chancellor, Professor Mosa Moshabela, talk say di future of di university no fit just dey depend on one technology. Di Minister of Higher Education, Buti Manamela, talk say AI suppose make education dey reach more people, wit wide AI literacy and better access to technology. UCT don stop to dey use AI-detection software, dem build dia own framework for how students and staff go dey use generative AI.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Fair access to generative AI for higher education na di first out of Wits AHEAD six pillars, and when minister talk say AI literacy, no be detection software, na im go bring fair access, na exactly wetin dis group policy and teaching work dey work on.

TimesLIVE · Established press

entry.title: Global Index on Responsible AI: 2026 Report
entry.summary:
Di Global Index on Responsible AI 2026, wey Global Center on AI Governance publish and launch for Geneva for July 2026, check governance for 135 kontris, dem use more than 68,000 data points wey dem collect between November 2023 and September 2025. Dem see say 126 out of di 135 kontris get at least one government policy or initiative about responsible AI, but dis one no too dey turn to protection wey dem fit enforce; AI literacy be one of di indicator wey dey perform well, 71 kontris, 53%, report say dem get framework, but less kontris get independent oversight body or monitoring system.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy na di sixth pillar of Wits AHEAD, and wetin dis index see, say AI literacy policy dey move pass di institution wey fit enforce am, na exactly di governance gap wey dis group policy work dey try close for higher education for Global South.

Global Center on AI Governance · Independent global governance research index

entry.title: Preparing future STEM educators: investigating artificial intelligence literacy among pre-service STEM teachers
entry.summary:
One study wey dem publish for di peer-reviewed journal STEM Education survey 541 teacher wey dey train for STEM for Lagos State, Nigeria, 345 women and 196 men, about dia AI literacy. Di teachers talk say dia general AI literacy high well, and di knowledge and understanding wey dem get about AI dey predict how dem go use am well; di study also see one gender gap wey dey significant for AI literacy, wey favour men pass women.

Why e matter for AHEAD: AI and data analytics for STEM and teacher education na di third pillar of Wits AHEAD, and dis gender gap wey dem see for trainee teachers for Lagos State na direct sign for how teacher-training programme for Global South suppose design dia own AI preparation.

STEM Education (AIMS Press) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Keeping the learning real: an integrated approach to academic integrity in the age of AI
entry.summary:
Wonkhe and di assessment service Studiosity review United Kingdom university policies and hold roundtable wit institutional leaders and students for September 2026 on academic integrity for this generative AI period. Di report, wey dem publish on 4 October 2026, find out say institutions dey move comot from policing AI use wit detection tools, dey go towards redesigned assessment, AI literacy and non-punitive ways to confirm say learning happen. E note say di academic integrity system still no get coherence, students no too trust am, as dem dey doubt whether institutions go believe dia own account of how dem use AI.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on generative AI for higher education, teaching, assessment and integrity, dis one be detailed, current account of how one major higher education system dey redesign assessment instead of just try to catch AI use, and e give practical framework to guide staff and students.

Wonkhe / Studiosity · UK higher education policy platform report, based on institutional policy review and sector roundtables

entry.title: Digital solidification: learning analytics, the panopticon, and data coloniality in South African higher education
entry.summary:
Singh, from University of Johannesburg, argue say learning analytics fit act like digital panopticon wey dey turn temporary setback, like load shedding or shortage of mobile data, into lasting deficit label for students, inside one framework of data coloniality. Di paper no treat learning analytics as something wey bad from inside out, but e warn say flags wey nobody challenge or update go worsen South Africa unequal material and language condition. E propose one social-justice framework wey dey rest on data amnesty, participatory algorithmic auditing and context-based way to read flags as prompt for support, no be punishment.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis one na direct South African, peer-reviewed critique of di predictive analytics tools wey dey central to Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and predictive analytics for student success, and e give di group pillar on responsible AI, ethics and equity solid safeguards to weigh before dem recommend early-warning systems.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Helpful or harmful? Generative AI dependence, self-reported critical thinking disposition, and self-perceived employability among business students
entry.summary:
Shojaei and colleagues survey 412 undergraduate business students across three universities for Oman on generative AI use, dependence, critical thinking disposition and how dem rate dia own employability. Students wey use AI more rate demsef as more employable, but students wey depend too much on AI get lower critical thinking, and dis one weaken di positive link between AI use and employability, until e lose meaning for students wey depend plenty on AI. Di authors conclude say di benefit depend on how person use AI with reflection and checking, no be how plenty dem use am, though di self-reported, cross-sectional design limit wetin dem fit claim as cause.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis one dey speak to Wits AHEAD pillar on AI, graduate capability and employability, e show say to depend on AI anyhow fit undercut di exact capability wey employers value, na one caution wey relevant for employability programmes across Global South.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Assessment practices resistant to inappropriate AI use in Open Distance eLearning: insights from Zimbabwe Open University
entry.summary:
Magwa and Zongozzi, from University of South Africa, interview lecturers, students and one quality assurance coordinator for Zimbabwe Open University Masvingo campus about wetin kain assessment no gree inappropriate use of generative AI. Dem find out say performance-based, reflective, oral and closely-watched formative assessment na di ones wey hard pass to complete dishonestly wit AI, though dis kain assessment fit cause wahala for lecturer workload and class size. Di authors caution say wetin dem find for one regional campus no fit generalise for di whole institution or open and distance learning overall.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis one give Global South, open and distance learning view on how to redesign assessment against generative AI misuse, for Wits AHEAD pillar on generative AI for higher education, and e relevant well well for open and distance programmes across di region.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Automated software scoring of senior school certificate examination mathematical items in economics using a contextual similarity model
entry.summary:
Olaoye, Owolabi and Olaoye test automated software wey dey score extended-response mathematics-based questions for senior secondary Economics for south-west Nigeria, dem take sample of 1,008 students from population of almost 275,000 candidates. Di software score match well well wit di one wey twelve trained human raters give, wit high average-measures intraclass correlation of 0.863. Di authors talk say di trial na only two items, and each rater score just 84 scripts, so dem need more testing before dem use am well well for exams like WAEC, NECO and NABTEB.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis one na concrete, STEM-related assessment analytics wey dem test for national exam level for West Africa, and e dey speak to Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and analytics for STEM and big education systems.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Six publishers agree to feed 20 million research papers to AI agents, in a pay-per-use deal
entry.summary:
Six scholarly publishers, including Sage, the BMJ Group and the Institute of Physics, don agree to let Swedish start-up Redpine dey feed more than 20 million peer-reviewed papers go AI agents for real time, Times Higher Education report on 6 October 2026. Di pay-per-use deal go dey pay publishers and authors anytime AI system use their work, and e cover journals for medicine, life sciences and physical sciences.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on Responsible AI, ethics, fair play and policy, dis deal be early test of how scholarly publishing fit make sure AI dey stand on verified research instead of guesswork, as dem still dey find out who go collect money anytime na machine, no be reader, dey do di citing.

Times Higher Education · Established press (Times Higher Education)

entry.title: Mystery-shopper study finds university enquiry replies 'costing enrolments', as ChatGPT outperforms
entry.summary:
One mystery-shopper study of 33 UK and 30 Australian universities, wey consultancy Edified and recruitment firm UniQuest do, and Times Higher Education report on 1 October 2026, see say na only 37 per cent of around 700 prospective-student enquiries get reply wey encourage dem to continue. Fifteen per cent of di enquiries no get answer at all, and dem rate ChatGPT reply dem say e dey quick, complete well well, and e fit convince pass wetin di universities dem write.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, dis study be strong reminder say institutions wey dey gather data for applicants must also use am well, because almost two out of three prospective students for di sample no see convincing human reply, wey one well-prompted AI fit don do better.

Times Higher Education · Established press (Times Higher Education), citing a study by Edified and UniQuest

entry.title: How computer-science students actually use large language models varies sharply by task, study finds
entry.summary:
One working paper wey dem post for arXiv on 1 October 2026 analyse how 211 undergraduates use large language models across seven modules of one computer-science problem-solving course. Students use di tools most for algorithms and web-development tasks, and least for software engineering, dem generally dey treat dem as assistants wey you go check, no be authority wey you go trust like that, dem dey verify output by testing for structured tasks and by web search for open-ended ones.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on Generative AI for higher education, di finding say verification habit dey change with di assignment, no be only with di student, be one concrete lesson for how academic integrity and assessment design go fit change task by task.

arXiv · Working paper (arXiv preprint)

entry.title: Cross-border virtual teamwork lifts intercultural readiness in data-analytics and machine-learning courses, study finds
entry.summary:
One working paper wey Sehrish Basir Nizamani and colleagues post for arXiv on 1 October 2026 describe one structured virtual exchange wey pair undergraduate computing students for United States and Pakistan together for six-phase, asynchronous data-analytics and machine-learning project. Students report consistently positive experience, and di researchers find out say cross-cultural communication, more pass technical skill, be di main thing wey shape how ready dem feel to work globally.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, dis study give one tested model for di cross-border, asynchronous teamwork wey computing students for Global South need to build both technical and intercultural capability without leaving house.

arXiv (accepted, IEEE Frontiers in Education 2026) · Working paper (arXiv preprint, accepted IEEE FIE 2026)

entry.title: Copenhagen university appoints an anthropologist, not a computer scientist, to lead its AI strategy
entry.summary:
University of Copenhagen don appoint anthropologist Morten Axel Pedersen as im first deputy prorector for AI, dem choose scholar wey sabi how people dey really behave over computer scientist, to lead 110 million Danish kroner strategy wey cover AI office, task force, laboratories and custom generative AI assistant. Pedersen, wey former direct di university Centre for Social Data Science, dey plan to review every course for di university within one year to decide how AI go dey used for each one, and e call im three-year post temporary scaffold wey dem go remove once each discipline get dia own rule.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1, wey be generative AI for higher education, teaching, assessment and integrity, Copenhagen choice show say how students and staff dey really use AI for practice, no be wetin policy paper talk alone, na di correct starting point for teaching and assessment reform. Wits AHEAD see am as proof say governance of AI for classroom na human matter as e be technical matter.

Times Higher Education (Seher Asaf) · Established press profile

entry.title: UK research network to redo grant review after AI triage rejected half of proposals
entry.summary:
CRANE, na UK cybersecurity research network wey dey University of Oxford and wey UK Research and Innovation dey support, don agree to redo di review of one funding call, after AI triage process reject almost half of di 179 proposals wey dem receive before any human reviewer see dem. Di network talk say dem use closed, secure system instead of public AI service, and say dem no go use any proposal data to train model; dem don pause di funding offer wey dem don already give, while dia panel dey reassess every application wey dem screen out.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, wey be responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, dis matter na warning say if institution use AI alone to guard research funding door without tell people or give dem chance to appeal, e fit lock out good work before person sef read am. Wits AHEAD point to di reassessment, no be di mistake alone, as di standard wey any institution wey dey use AI for high-stakes review suppose follow.

Times Higher Education (Frances Jones) · Established press investigation

entry.title: Tshwane University of Technology dialogue presses South Africa to move from AI strategy to implementation
entry.summary:
Tshwane University of Technology im Institute for the Future of Work host dia fifth annual Future of Work Dialogue for Pretoria, e bring government, academics and industry together under di theme of pushing Africa resilient future through AI-enabled innovation. Senior director Tseliso Mohlomi talk say South Africa must move from AI strategy and talk-talk to real action, e mention cybersecurity, cloud computing, AI literacy and data engineering as di skills wey dem need sharp sharp. Di dialogue repeat one proposal, wey never happen since last year meeting, for National AI Implementation Council wey go coordinate government, universities and industry to reach outcome wey dem fit measure.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 4, wey be AI, graduate human capability, employability and just transitions, how di dialogue dey push for action instead of more policy talk match Wits AHEAD worry well well, say strategy paper alone no dey create job. One coordinating council like dis one wey dem propose na di structure wey go match university training to di skills wey dem name, wey dey change fast.

iAfrica.com (Thebe Mabanga, Inside Education) · Established press report on a university-hosted policy dialogue

entry.title: Liberia advances a national education data system to inform real-time decisions
entry.summary:
Liberia Ministry of Education don finish national stakeholder meeting on new policy for Education Management Information System (EMIS), wey African Union dey support through im Pan-African Institute for Education and Development. Deputy Minister Thomas Momo Parker talk say di kontri need correct, up-to-date data to plan, budget and take decision, as di ministry dey bring back im Annual School Census and dey introduce new booklet wey law talk say school must use to keep record. Di meeting, wey dem hold for Monrovia with European Union, UNESCO, Plan International Liberia and UNICEF, see gap for data governance, infrastructure, technical capacity and money matter.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 5, wey be analytics and data for education system and decision making, Liberia own move show say strong national data foundation, no be algorithm alone, na di base wey any Global South system need before dem fit trust prediction tools or dashboard. Wits AHEAD dey follow dis kain groundwork as di thing wey must first dey before di analytics wey dem dey study elsewhere fit work.

African Newspage (Ministry of Education, Republic of Liberia) · National government announcement

entry.title: A college president on harnessing AI in education without cutting corners
entry.summary:
Colby College president David Greene tell ABC News how di American liberal arts college dey use artificial intelligence for teaching and learning, for one way wey e call ethical and wey no dey cut corners. Na short account, from di person wey dey lead am, about how institution fit lead on AI.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1, generative AI for higher education, e show one university leader wey dey treat AI as something wey dem go shape on purpose, no be only something to police, and na di same stand wey Wits AHEAD dey argue for African universities.

ABC News · ABC News (US national broadcaster)

entry.title: What should a university be in the age of AI? SABC News on the first Times Higher Education summit in Africa
entry.summary:
Before di Times Higher Education World Academic Summit, wey University of Cape Town host from 29 September to 1 October, di first one wey dem ever hold for African soil, SABC News ask wetin university suppose look like as AI dey change how people dey work, learn and create knowledge. UCT Deputy Vice-Chancellor for Research and Internationalisation, Prof Thokozani Majozi, talk about di summit theme, "Knowledge, justice and futures: Universities in the age of intelligence", and di role wey universities get pass just to produce graduates.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 4, graduate capability and transitions, di summit question about wetin universities owe graduates and society as AI dey reshape work na di group own question, and now dem dey ask am for South African stage.

SABC News · SABC News (public broadcaster)

entry.title: African scholarship is building a decolonial agenda for AI in university classrooms, systematic review finds
entry.summary:
One systematic review for Trends in Higher Education map 25 studies from 2010 to 2025 on decoloniality, artificial intelligence and university classrooms for African higher education. Research output increase quick quick after 2020 around three themes: epistemic injustice and curriculum, algorithmic coloniality and data extractivism, and di teaching changes wey generative AI dey demand. Most of di research dey for South Africa, and new Pan-African work on AI for African languages dey come up. Di authors find say one decolonial AI research agenda wey hold together dey take shape, but empirical evidence still small for now.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI and policy, e name di questions of whose knowledge and whose language AI dey carry enter African classrooms, and e show how di empirical base still thin, one gap wey research for Wits School of Education fit help fill.

Trends in Higher Education (MDPI) · Peer-reviewed systematic review

entry.title: AI emerges as a distinct part of the student academic experience in a survey of 2,403 Bolivian undergraduates
entry.summary:
One study of 2,403 undergraduates for one private university for Bolivia, wey dem publish for Education Sciences, validate one 31-item survey of di academic experience and find say how students talk say dem dey use AI for dia learning stand as im own separate factor, together with engagement, critical thinking, teaching quality and dedication. Di AI use wey students report connect positively with academic engagement and with communication, ethical and critical-thinking skills; di authors stress say di instrument dey measure perception, no be learning outcomes.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar 1, generative AI for higher education, one validated instrument from Global South wey treat AI use as part of how students dey experience university na practical tool wey di group fit adapt for South African student surveys, with di authors warning say e dey measure perception, no be learning.

Education Sciences (MDPI) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Oxford let OpenAI train AI models on Bodleian Library texts, the Guardian reports
entry.summary:
Papers wey Guardian newspaper see show say University of Oxford allow OpenAI to digitize old texts from im Bodleian Library, including 125,000 scans of PhD theses from di 19th and 20th century, plus 10,000 Tudor-time broadside ballads, to help train im AI models. Oxford partnership with OpenAI, wey dem announce for 2025, dem talk say na project to make rare texts available for more people; dem no mention say di scans go dey used to train OpenAI data. Internal meeting notes show say some governance committee members talk worry about reputation risk and di energy cost of AI, but Oxford talk say di material na small-small one, no dey under copyright again, and dem go publish am online for di next few months.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar six, responsible AI, ethics and policy, dis matter na warning for any university, for Global South or for Oxford, wey dey give AI company access to im archive or data: if di university no talk am well-well how dem go use di material, a genuine access project fit end up look like one quiet data-supply deal, and dat na exactly di transparency gap wey Wits AHEAD dey push institutions to close before dem sign.

The Guardian (Ethan Penny and Dan Milmo) · Established press investigation

entry.title: University of Ghana approves an AI policy and a compulsory digital literacy course for every student
entry.summary:
University of Ghana Council approve one AI policy wey go cover di whole school, afta one internal survey find out say students and staff no get enough training, dia access to AI tools dey limited, and pipo dey worry about accuracy, academic integrity and ethics. Di vice-chancellor, Professor Nana Aba Appiah Amfo, announce am for di school graduation for Accra, where 1,884 students graduate, say di university go also make sure say every student, starting from next academic year, go take one new compulsory course for digital literacy and applied AI, alongside one separate Teaching and Learning Policy.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar one, generative AI for higher education, how one government university dey move from just guideline paper to compulsory AI literacy course for every graduate, wey dem build based on dia own evidence of wia students and staff dey struggle, na di kain structured, whole-campus response wey Wits AHEAD dey look for across di continent, instead of policy wey dey only exist on paper.

University of Ghana (policy document); Ghanaian Times · University policy document

entry.title: OECD finds generative AI use nearly universal in higher education but only one in five institutions has a formal policy
entry.summary:
One OECD report, Policies supporting responsible and systematic GenAI adoption in higher education, wey dem publish for di OECD Education Spotlights series, find out say generative AI use among university students don almost reach everybody, e rise from 66% of UK undergraduates for 2024 to 95% for 2026, with 86% of students for one 16-country survey dey use am now. But only 19% of higher education institutions worldwide get formal generative AI policy for 2025, even as 42% more dey draft dia own, and only 17% of academic staff worldwide dem count as advanced or expert users.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For pillar six, responsible AI, ethics and policy, di gap wey OECD measure, between everyday use wey almost reach everybody and formal governance for just one university out of five, na exactly di gap wey Wits AHEAD dey try close, and e dey remind us say to adopt AI tools and to govern am well-well na two different work, wey most universities never finish any of dem.

University World News (Karen MacGregor), reporting an OECD report · Intergovernmental research report, reported by established press
